assumptions: A sufficiently large set of European EEG or sleep-device teams has recurring validation needs that can be served by one narrowly standardized endpoint.
At least one clinic and qualified principal-investigator team can deliver the protocol at terms compatible with sponsor-funded project economics.
Participant, sponsor, clinic, GDPR, and study-governance constraints can permit reuse of narrowly defined derived metrics without exposing sponsor-confidential information.
The founder will not commit material cohort expenditure or assume regulated clinical responsibilities before the stated funding, clinic, and governance gates are contractually satisfied.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A costed protocol and signed clinic/PI responsibility allocation; written protocol-specific regulatory and data-rights opinions; and, most importantly, at least two noncompeting sponsors signing deposits that cover external cohort costs at a demonstrated price, followed by evidence of usable-signal yield, gross margin, repeat demand, and lawful benchmark reuse.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Pooling a fixed validation endpoint across noncompeting device sponsors could reduce duplicated cohort cost while producing more comparable reference metrics. The insight is coherent, but the packet does not establish that sponsors share enough timing, protocol, or data-rights interests to cooperate.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: New devices and algorithm versions plausibly need credible clinical comparison, and existing specialist providers indicate a real category of demand. There is no direct evidence that buyers want this consortium format, will accept a common endpoint, or will prepay the proposed work.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Deposits before launch and milestone payments are sensible cash-risk controls, while standardized analysis could eventually carry attractive margins. However, pricing, clinic and recruitment costs, gross margin, CAC, sales-cycle cost, retention, benchmark revenue, and owner earnings are all unmeasured; the 175,000 PLN planning requirement also exceeds free founder capital absent sponsor funding.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: A single EEG or sleep endpoint is focused enough to test and aligns with the founder's expertise. The economically reachable sponsor count and project cadence are not quantified, and requiring two noncompeting sponsors with synchronized needs may make the effective beachhead much smaller than the broader wearable-validation market.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A repeat protocol at a Central-European clinic could create a narrow specialist position, but VivoSense, Empatica, TNO, and Delve already cover much of the validation and operations stack. No exclusive clinic access, superior outcome, lower verified price, or sponsor preference establishes a credible path to dominating the beachhead.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful repeatable endpoint could extend to device versions, adjacent endpoints, additional sponsors, and other geographies. Each extension may require new clinical validation, regulatory analysis, and rights negotiations, so expansion is plausible but not automatically leveraged.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Comparable derived metrics and accumulated protocol failure modes could compound if lawful reuse rights and repeated cohorts are secured. Those rights are presently unknown, the first dataset does not exist, clinic exclusivity is absent, and established providers could imitate a successful consortium structure.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Shared fixed costs and a common benchmark could offer better comparability or price than separate studies. Neither advantage is quantified, and sponsors may value bespoke protocols, confidentiality, or an established CRO's trust more than pooled savings.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Wearable clinical validation is an active category, but the packet supplies no demand-growth evidence specific to this wedge. EHDS does not create near-term access or exclusivity and its relevant clinical-study and cohort provisions phase in later, while current GDPR and device-study obligations add friction now.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The proposed bounded founder-led consortium sale identifies a clear target and paid event. It nevertheless requires coordinating at least two sponsors plus a clinic without a signed channel, lead pipeline, measured conversion, or sales cycle, and it is unusually trust-heavy for the founder's time and social-energy constraints.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder has relevant EEG, neuroscience, and data-science fit, and the no-launch gates limit uncontrolled capital exposure. Execution still depends on qualified clinical leadership, ethics and potentially URPL processes, privacy and quality ownership, recruitment, signal quality, multi-party contracts, and rights allocation while the founder keeps a full-time job.

highest_value_structural_change: Remove the need for two sponsors to synchronize before the first sale: structure an anchor-sponsored fixed protocol in which one sponsor fully funds its validation, receives sponsor-specific outputs, and contractually permits only defined nonconfidential derived metrics to seed a reusable benchmark; add later sponsors asynchronously under the same protocol, with no launch unless the anchor price covers external costs.
main_structural_strength: The model converts its largest uncertainties into explicit pre-launch gates: no participant operations or material cohort spending occurs until sponsors fund the study, qualified clinic roles accept responsibility, the regulatory route is documented, and benchmark rights are contractually bounded.
primary_score_limiter: The business requires simultaneous sponsor, clinic, regulatory, and data-rights commitments, yet there is no evidence that sponsors will coordinate on one endpoint or prepay at economics that leave attractive recurring margins.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Established providers already market overlapping wearable protocol, analytics, clinical validation, regulatory, quality-control, and participant-operation capabilities, while no sponsor has evidenced a perceived Central-European consortium gap or accepted its price and shared-benchmark terms.
